entries.title: Ezekiel 30:1
segments:
. CONTINUATION OF THE PROPHECIES AGAINST EGYPT. 
 
    Two distinct messages: (1) At
, a repetition of
, with fuller details of lifelike distinctness. The date is probably not long after that mentioned in

, on the eve of Nebuchadnezzar's march against Egypt after subjugating Tyre. (2) A vision relating directly to Pharaoh and the overthrow of his kingdom; communicated at an earlier date, the seventh of the first month of the eleventh year. Not a year after the date in
, and three months before the taking of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:2
segments: 2. Woe worth the day!--that is, Alas for the day!

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:3
segments: 3. the time of the heathen--namely, for taking vengeance on them. The judgment on Egypt is the beginning of a world-wide judgment on all the heathen enemies of God (

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:4
segments: 4. pain--literally, "pangs with trembling as of a woman in childbirth."

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:5
segments: 5. the mingled people--the mercenary troops of Egypt from various lands, mostly from the interior of Africa (compare
). Even they shall not escape (

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:6
segments: 6. from the tower of Syene--(see on

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:7
segments: 7. in the midst of ... countries ... desolate--Egypt shall fare no better than they (

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:9
segments: 9. messengers ... in ships to ... Ethiopians-- (
). The cataracts interposing between them and Egypt should not save them. Egyptians "fleeing from before Me" in My execution of judgment, as "messengers" in "skiffs" ("vessels of bulrushes,"

) shall go up the Nile as far as navigable, to announce the advance of the Chaldeans. 
 
    as in the day of Egypt--The day of Ethiopia's "pain" shall come shortly, as Egypt's day came.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:10
segments: 10. the multitude--the large population.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:12
segments: 12. rivers--the artificial canals made from the Nile for irrigation. The drying up of these would cause scarcity of grain, and so prepare the way for the invaders (

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:13
segments:
13. Noph--Memphis, the capital of Middle Egypt, and the stronghold of "idols." Though no record exists of Nebuchadnezzar's "destroying" these, we know from HERODOTUS and others, that Cambyses took Pelusium, the key of Egypt, by placing before his army dogs, cats, &c., all held sacred in Egypt, so that no Egyptian would use any weapon against them. He slew Apis, the sacred ox, and burnt other idols of Egypt. 
 
    no more a prince--referring to the anarchy that prevailed in the civil wars between Apries and Amasis at the time of Nebuchadnezzar's invasion. There shall no more be a prince of the land of Egypt, ruling the whole country; or, no independent prince.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:14
segments: 14. Pathros--Upper Egypt, with "No" or Thebes its capital (famed for its stupendous buildings, of which grand ruins remain), in antithesis to Zoan or Tanis, a chief city in Lower Egypt, within the Delta.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:15
segments: 15. Sin--that is, Pelusium, the frontier fortress on the northeast, therefore called "the strength (that is, the key) of Egypt." It stands in antithesis to No or Thebes at the opposite end of Egypt; that is, I will afflict Egypt from one end to the other.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:16
segments: 16. distresses daily--MAURER translates, "enemies during the day," that is, open enemies who do not wait for the covert of night to make their attacks (compare
). However, the Hebrew, though rarely, is sometimes rendered (see
) as in English Version.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:17
segments: 17. Aven--meaning "vanity" or "iniquity": applied, by a slight change of the Hebrew name, to On or Heliopolis, in allusion to its idolatry. Here stood the temple of the sun, whence it was called in Hebrew, Beth-shemesh (
, "daughters shall go into captivity" [MAURER].

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:18
segments: 18. Tehaphnehes--called from the queen of Egypt mentioned in
. The same as Daphne, near Pelusium, a royal residence of the Pharaohs (
). Called Hanes

). 
 
    break ... the yokes of Egypt--that is, the tyrannical supremacy which she exercised over other nations. Compare "bands of their yoke" (

). 
 
    a cloud--namely, of calamity.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:20
segments: 20. Here begins the earlier vision, not long after that in the twenty-ninth chapter, about three months before the taking of Jerusalem, as to Pharaoh and his kingdom.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:21
segments: 21. broken ... arm of Pharaoh-- (
). Referring to the defeat which Pharaoh-hophra sustained from the Chaldeans, when trying to raise the siege of Jerusalem (
); and previous to the deprivation of Pharaoh-necho of all his conquests from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates (
); also to the Egyptian disaster in Cyrene.

entries.title: Ezekiel 30:22
segments: 22. arms--Not only the "one arm" broken already (

) was not to be healed, but the other two should be broken. Not a corporal wound, but a breaking of the power of Pharaoh is intended. 
 
    cause ... sword to fall out of ... hand--deprive him of the resources of making war.
